title: Cardamonin activates AMPK/FOXO3a/Nrf-2 axis to ameliorate oxidative stress in hyperlipidemia induced cardiac injury in mice.
authors: Yang, Wenjia; Jiao, Qiuhong; Chen, Jiahong; Xu, Longwu; Han, Haoyu; Feng, Junjie; Wang, Xinyu; Wang, Tao; Meng, Chun
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物Cardamonin通过AMPK/FOXO3a/Nrf-2通路缓解高脂血症心肌氧化损伤，属纯药理学与动物实验，无蛋白质-DNA互作、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hyperlipidemia (HLP) is a prevalent metabolic disorder that induces myocardial injury through prolonged oxidative stress. Cardamonin (CAR), a natural chalcone from the Zingiberaceae family, is recognised for its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities; however, its specific role and underlying mechanisms in cardiovascular protection against HLP remain to be fully elucidated. This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of CAR on HLP-induced cardiac damage. METHODS AND RESULTS: An integrated approach combining network pharmacology and molecular docking was first employed to identify potential targets. Subsequently, in vivo experiments were conducted using C57BL/6J mice (n = 6 per group). HLP-induced cardiac injury models were established and treated with CAR. Network pharmacology and docking results revealed the AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)/forkhead box protein O3a (FOXO3a)/nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf-2) signalling axis as a key target of CAR. The in vivo results demonstrated that CAR treatment significantly activated this pathway, thereby upregulating the expression of downstream antioxidant genes and alleviating oxidative stress. These molecular changes resulted in a significant reduction in myocardial histological damage and increased the expression of cardiac markers in HLP mice compared with those in the untreated group. CONCLUSIONS: CAR attenuates HLP-induced myocardial injury by activating the AMPK/FOXO3a/Nrf-2 axis to suppress oxidative stress. These findings provide new evidence for the therapeutic potential of CAR as a cardioprotective agent for managing hyperlipidemia-related complications.
abstract_zh: 背景：高脂血症（HLP）是一种常见的代谢性疾病，通过长期氧化应激诱导心肌损伤。豆蔻明（CAR），一种来自姜科（Zingiberaceae）的天然查尔酮，以其抗氧化和抗炎活性而闻名；然而，其在心血管保护中对抗HLP的具体作用及潜在机制尚未完全阐明。本研究旨在探讨CAR对HLP诱导的心脏损伤的保护作用。方法与结果：首先采用网络药理学和分子对接 (molecular docking) 相结合的综合方法识别潜在靶点。随后，使用C57BL/6J小鼠（每组n = 6）进行体内实验。建立HLP诱导的心脏损伤模型，并用CAR处理。网络药理学和对接结果显示，AMP活化蛋白激酶 (AMPK)/叉头框蛋白O3a (FOXO3a)/核因子E2相关因子2 (Nrf-2) 信号轴是CAR的关键靶点。体内结果表明，CAR处理显著激活了该通路，从而上调下游抗氧化基因的表达并减轻氧化应激。与未处理组相比，这些分子变化导致HLP小鼠心肌组织学损伤显著减少，并增加心脏标志物的表达。结论：CAR通过激活AMPK/FOXO3a/Nrf-2轴抑制氧化应激，从而减轻HLP诱导的心肌损伤。这些发现为CAR作为心脏保护剂管理高脂血症相关并发症的治疗潜力提供了新证据。
